title: Object Detection & Tracking on Zynq
summary: An embedded-vision study taking object detection from MATLAB and OpenCV prototypes to an HLS core integrated on a Zynq platform.
problem: Explore an implementation path for image processing that combines programmable logic with software-controlled interfaces.
approach: Developed the algorithm in MATLAB and C++/OpenCV.
Created a processing core through the HLS workflow.
Integrated the design with Vivado and Xilinx SDK on the Zynq board.
outcome: An embedded-vision implementation workflow with a system concept diagram and original algorithm and comparison demonstrations.
hardware: Spartan-6 and Raspberry Pi as platforms considered

sections.title: A vision algorithm on an embedded platform
body: My undergraduate work explored object detection and tracking on a Zynq-based platform. The project connects image-processing software with the tools needed to build and integrate programmable logic.

sections.title: From software to an HLS core
body: The development path began with MATLAB, continued with a C++/OpenCV implementation and then moved into HLS. Vivado and Xilinx SDK were used to transfer the design into the board-level workflow.

sections.title: Finding a target colour
body: For the colour-based detection step, pixels in an incoming frame are compared with a selected colour range and matching locations are marked. The frame-search demonstration makes this operation visible.

sections.title: The board-level system
body: The concept diagram connects the camera/video path, ZYBO board, display and host interface. The platform uses a Zynq XC7Z010CLG400-1; the research also considered Spartan-6 and Raspberry Pi implementation options.

sections.title: Different implementations, one question
body: The comparison recording presents the timing of three implementations side by side. Additional Sobel-filter and frame-search demonstrations show related parts of the vision-development process. The public source repository contains MATLAB, OpenCV, HLS, SDK and Vivado materials alongside the Persian report.

strength: An algorithm carried from software into Zynq.
contribution: My undergraduate work carried the vision algorithm from MATLAB prototypes through C++/OpenCV to an HLS core and Zynq board-integration workflow.
result: An embedded-vision implementation workflow with a system concept diagram and original algorithm and comparison demonstrations.
decisionNotes: The development sequence used MATLAB, C++/OpenCV and HLS before board integration with Vivado and Xilinx SDK. Colour-range comparisons expose a simple frame-search operation alongside the Sobel-filter demonstration.
validationNotes: A recording compares three implementations; separate recordings show Sobel filtering and target-colour frame search. Hardware, workload and measurement conditions are not fully documented here, so the recording is not presented as a reproducible speedup benchmark.
